_readme: German uses du. `dbcx retrieval assess` fills {documents} (extracted client documents), {pages} (approx. pages = estimated tokens / 500) and {download_mb} (the one-time download in MB) and prints the message when the assessment is `recommended`; the orchestrator asks the user with exactly this text (Markdown kept).
message:
Your material is quite large: **{documents} documents, roughly {pages} pages**. That is more than the agents can read in full, so they will search it.

I recommend adding a **smarter search tool (model2vec)**. It finds passages that mean the same thing even when they are worded differently or written in the other language – for example "Faktura" when the agents look for "invoicing".

**What this means for you:** a one-time download of about **{download_mb} MB** (it takes a few minutes and then uses about 260 MB on your computer). Your client's documents never leave your computer. I'll take care of everything – you only need to say yes.

**If you'd rather not:** we stick with the standard search, which only finds the exact words. The run works the same way, but in our tests the right passage was missed more often (about 4 in 10 searches instead of 1 in 4). That slightly raises the risk that something in your material contradicts a statement and nobody notices. You can add the tool later at any time.

Shall I install it? (yes / no)
